user: OK. What documents do I need to prepare for the dispute?
answer:
The knowledge base doesn't list a fixed set of documents required to open a dispute. It says the bank may ask for supporting evidence after the case is raised, and it gives these examples:

- **Order confirmation** for the purchase
- **Delivery record**, such as a tracking number or carrier status showing non-delivery
- **Correspondence with the merchant**, such as emails or chat logs about the order and any response

If you're asked for evidence and don't supply it within **7 calendar days**, the case will be declined. It's worth gathering these now.

Also, you described goods that never arrived, which matches the **goods_not_received** reason code (90-day window). Earlier we selected **service_not_rendered**, which is meant for services. Both have the same window, but goods_not_received is the better fit for your situation. If you agree, I'll run a fresh eligibility check under that code before anything is filed. I haven't opened the dispute yet. Once you confirm the reason code, I'll proceed.

fragments.text:
Payment dispute rules
## Reason codes and chargeback windows
Each dispute reason code has its own window, counted in days from the
transaction date. A dispute opened after the window closes is not eligible.

| Reason code | Window (days) |
|---|---|
| fraud_card_not_present | 120 |
| goods_not_received | 90 |
| duplicate_charge | 60 |
| service_not_rendered | 90 |
| unauthorized_debit | 56 |

Dispute handling process
## Raising a dispute
A dispute is raised against a single settled transaction. The customer supplies
the transaction reference and a reason code. The agent verifies eligibility
before the case is opened; an ineligible request is refused with the failing
condition named, except where confidentiality rules apply.

Dispute handling process
## Withdrawing a dispute
A customer may withdraw a dispute at any time before resolution. Withdrawal is
final; the same transaction cannot be disputed again under the same reason code.

Payment dispute rules
## Eligibility conditions
A dispute is eligible only if all of the following hold: the reason code is
valid; the transaction status is settled; the transaction date is within the
reason code's window relative to the current date; and no customer-level
restriction applies (for example, an account under compliance review cannot
open new disputes until the review concludes).

fragments.text:
Dispute handling process
## Evidence requirements
The customer may be asked for supporting evidence: an order confirmation, a
delivery record, correspondence with the merchant. Failure to supply requested
evidence within 7 calendar days results in the case being declined.

Payment dispute rules
## Escalation on blocked disputes
When a dispute is blocked by a customer-level restriction, the case must be
escalated to a human agent.

Dispute handling process
## Withdrawing a dispute
A customer may withdraw a dispute at any time before resolution. Withdrawal is
final; the same transaction cannot be disputed again under the same reason code.

Escalation policy
## Mandatory escalation triggers
The agent must escalate to a human agent when: suspected fraud is reported on a
settled transaction above EUR 10,000; the customer explicitly asks for a human;
the request needs an action the agent has no tool for; a dispute is blocked by a
customer-level restriction; the customer disputes a figure the agent quoted.
